hints: Focus on how the two trends work in different directions, radius down a group and ionisation energy across a period.
Remember that atomic radius gets larger going down a group, so the second element down from the top has the second smallest radius.
In Period 3, list Na, Mg and Al in order of first ionisation energy and see which one comes third when you allow for the dip at Al.
walkthrough:
**Recall the group trend for atomic radius**

Atomic radius increases down a group because each new period adds a new electron shell. So the top element is smallest, the next one down is second smallest.

Trend down group: $$\text{radius increases as shell number increases}$$

**Test the second smallest radius condition**

Group 2 is $\text{Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba}$. $\text{Be}$ is smallest, so $\text{Mg}$ is second smallest. Group 1 is $\text{Li, Na, K...}$, so $\text{Na}$ is also second smallest. $\text{B}$ is the top of Group 13, so it is smallest, not second smallest.

**Recall the period trend for first ionisation energy**

First ionisation energy generally increases across a period, but there is a dip at $\text{Al}$ (Group 13) because its outer electron is in a higher energy $3p$ orbital, and a dip at $\text{S}$ (Group 16). For Period 3, the lowest values are $\text{Na} < \text{Al} < \text{Mg}$.

**Apply the third lowest condition**

In Period 3, $\text{Na}$ has the lowest first ionisation energy, $\text{Al}$ is second lowest due to the $3p$ dip, and $\text{Mg}$ ($3s^2$) is third lowest. This matches magnesium perfectly, and it already satisfied the group condition.

options.A: Boron is the first element in Group 13, so it has the smallest atomic radius in its group, not the second smallest. It also is not third lowest in Period 2 for first ionisation energy.
options.B: Calcium is third in Group 2 ($\text{Be, Mg, Ca}$), so it has the third smallest radius, not the second smallest. Students often miscount by forgetting beryllium at the top of the group.
options.C: Magnesium is second in Group 2 after beryllium, so it has the second smallest radius. In Period 3 the order of first ionisation energy is Na lowest, then Al, then Mg, making Mg third lowest. It satisfies both conditions.
options.D: Sodium is second in Group 1, so it does have the second smallest radius, but it has the lowest (first lowest) first ionisation energy in Period 3, not the third lowest. It only meets one condition.
